description: Checks a restaurant's own website as the online check on restaurantdoctorai.com does: secure (https) and on its own address, made for phones, a menu written as text that phones and Google can read, online orders on its own terms or only through delivery apps, the address, hours and phone written on the page, tap to call, a way to get in touch, email sign-up and gift cards, what Google reads (a headline, title and description, not hidden from search, restaurant structured data), the preview a shared link shows, the page's text, story, questions, reviews, photo descriptions and social links, and Google's phone speed test with its measures one by one and real visitors' speed when Google has it (15 to 40 seconds; phoneSpeed: false skips it). Returns the score and grade, each area's score, the three checks to fix first with what to do about each, what a basic AI reader can tell about each question in a word, and a link to the full online check, which adds the Google listing, every check with what to fix, the reasons and places nearby on the website. A check it couldn't make (a page drawn by scripts, a security screen instead of the page) is left out of the score, never failed; every check, its points and where its facts come from are listed at https://restaurantdoctorai.com/online-check/checks. Takes only the website address. The website isn't stored; only an anonymous daily count of checks is kept.

phoneSpeed.description: Whether to run Google's phone speed test too (the default). It takes 15 to 40 seconds; false skips it.

website.description: The restaurant's own website address, such as joesdiner.com or https://www.joesdiner.com. Not a DoorDash, Uber Eats or Google Maps page.

name: restaurantdoctor_check_website

aiAnswers.description: What a basic AI reader can tell from the home page and at most one menu page: whether AI can get in, what the restaurant sells, its prices, hours, phone and address, and how guests can order or book. Not part of the score. Assistants differ, and some run scripts. No score, and no promise of being recommended.

state.description: found (written on the page, which doesn't mean every assistant gets it), missing (not found) or unknown (can't tell). For whether AI can get in, found means no block in the site's robots.txt or tags (a firewall we can't see could still turn crawlers away) and missing means the site's own rules block or limit it.

word.description: The state in words, as the owner reads it: Found, Not found, Can't tell, Not blocked by your rules, Linked.

areas.description: The score for the website and for its speed on a phone.

anyOf.description: Nothing could be checked here, or the phone speed test was skipped.

toFix.description: How many checks in this area need work.

checked.description: How many checks could be made. One that couldn't (a page drawn by scripts, a security screen) is left out of the score, never failed.

fixFirst.description: Up to three checks to fix first, most important first.

fullCheckUrl.description: The full online check on restaurantdoctorai.com: adds the Google listing, every check with what to fix, the reasons behind each answer and the places nearby.

meaning.description: What the grade means, in a line for the owner.

needWork.description: How many of the checks need work. The full online check names each one.

phoneSpeedSkipped.description: Google's phone speed test wasn't run, because phoneSpeed was false. It isn't in the score.

score.description: 0 to 100, from the website and phone-speed checks only (the full check adds the Google listing).

website.description: Where the site answered after redirects: its scheme and host only, such as https://www.joesdiner.com.

title: Check a restaurant's website
